- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥15 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots downward; apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid premature reversal.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force a 1–2 day mean reversion bias toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price volatility; add 2–3% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment is mixed (alternating ±1.00), model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values before projecting next 30d.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after forecast peak, model overreacted; apply “recovery lag” rule: delay next forecast peak by 2–3 days if sentiment remains negative.
